newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian credit rating remains unchanged at DB3a.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian credit rating remains unchanged at DB3a.

text.p: Slovenia's credit rating remained stable in November and it is unlikely to change in the wake of last weekend's general election, credit agency Dun and Bradstreet's (D&B) Ljubljana representative said on Wednesday.
"With a degree of currency stability, the government is confident that it can reduce inflation over time," the agency said in its latest Risk & Payment Review.
D&B gave Slovenia an unchanged DB3a credit rating for November, placing it second in the region behind the Czech Republic and ahead of Poland.
"However, inflatory pressures do remain at present," it noted.
In October, Slovenia's annual inflation rate rose to 9.7 percent from 9.4 in September.
The government has forecast annual inflation to remain below 10 percent to year-end despite expected hikes in energy prices. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
